steps.relative: Every major key shares its signature with a minor key, its relative minor, whose tonic is degree 6 of the major scale, three half steps below the major tonic. {c} major and {a} minor have no sharps or flats; {g} major and {e} minor have one sharp. On the circle, it’s the inner ring.
steps.nameIt: Go down three half steps from the major tonic to name its relative minor.
steps.build: Now find its tonic on the keys, from the major tonic given.
steps.twoKeys: So one signature means two keys. To tell which, look at where the music comes to rest: the last note, usually the tonic, settles it.
steps.backUp: Now the other way: go up three half steps from the minor tonic.
